title: The Silent Background Thread Crash
pattern: Spawning asynchronous background tasks or threads without registering handlers to propagate, log, or restart on failure.
why_bad: The main process remains running and responding to pings, but critical background services (like caching, log-saver daemons, or replication tasks) have crashed permanently, leading to silent data rot or stale states [192, 638].
detection: Spawning asynchronous tasks without registering telemetry metrics, panicking on join failure, or exporting thread exit states.
fix: Connect background thread outcomes directly to application lifecycle managers, ensuring task crashes either terminate the process or log error metrics that trigger immediate automated restarts.
source: *Implementing Domain-Driven Design*, Chapter 8 [192, 638]; *Kill It with Fire*, Chapter 10 [487, 632].
